history.period: c. 1167-1168 CE (per epigraphical record at the site)
history.summary: Shiva temple in Malhar, Malhar's temples belong to the 10th-11th century Kalachuri building phase. An inscription dates its construction to 1167-1168 CE in the reign of Jajalladeva II of the Haihaya dynasty, built by a Brahmin named Somraj of Kumhati; the inscription names it Kedareshwar, dedicated to Lord Kedar. The west-facing shrine has the Shivalinga set on a lower level than the pillared mandapa (reached by steps), which likely gave the temple its name 'Pataleshwar' (lord of the netherworld). The doorjambs carry Ganga, Yamuna and dvarapala figures; the site also yielded Jain memorials during excavation. It is a nationally important monument under the ASI. Note: 'Cave Temple' in the CSV is a descriptor of the sunken sanctum; it is not a rock-cut cave. Malhar itself was Sarabhapur/Mallar, an ancient capital of South Kosala, with occupation from c. 1000 BCE through the Ratnapura Kalachuri period.

name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple, Malhar
town_description: Malhar (ancient Sarabhapur, also Mallar or Mallari) is a small town in Masturi tehsil, Bilaspur district, Chhattisgarh, about 40 km by road from Bilaspur. It was a major city and capital of South Kosala in the 1st millennium CE. Excavations have revealed remains from c. 1000 BCE through the Kalachuri period, and the town is on the ASI's list of monuments of national importance; a Government of India museum houses its sculpture collection.
